pages: You arrived after dark with a bag and Nell's address. The key was under the third flowerpot, just as she'd said.
You remember carrying your things upstairs. After that, mostly the bed. Now there's daylight across the floor and someone moving about below.
A corner of paper peeks out from under the mug on the desk.

lines: There's bread in the tin. I'll be back around lunchtime.
The little one on the shelf is Hotaru. I've been out on calls all week, so she's mostly been asleep.
The terminal on the desk is linked to Hotaru. Send her a hello if you need a hand.

stairs.dormant: The stairs lead down to Nell's workshop. Hotaru is still dozing on the shelf.
stairs.awake: The stairs lead down to Nell's workshop.
stairs.tablet: Nell’s slate is still on the bed.

after_greeting.title: Your first page is saved
after_greeting.hint: Hotaru is up. Nell's workshop is downstairs; the job board and repair benches are worth a look.

street_doors: Nell has left the street doors latched while she's out. The stairs lead back to your room.

workshop_after_greeting.title: The morning round is ready
workshop_after_greeting.hint: Your routines are saved. Nell is still out on calls; the workshop lights are yours to try.

pages.speaker: narration
pages.text: The workshop is warmer than the loft. A knot of shavings has collected beneath the vice; beside it, someone has set a stool out from the bench.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: Nell made room for you last night.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: She was down here after you’d gone to bed.

choices.reply: At the long bench. Keep the narrow drawer clear; she opens it with her knee.

choices.text: Is there anything I can do?
choices.reply: There’s a ticket on the board. She pinned it before she went out.
You were asleep before she’d found the spare key.

pages.speaker: narration
pages.text: Hotaru looks past you towards the stairs.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: Nell left a ticket for the stair light. It was my job to put it on.

pages.speaker: narration
pages.text: The ticket is soft along one edge. It has spent some time in a coat pocket.

pages.speaker: ticket
pages.text:
STAIR LIGHT
Relay replaced. Fitting checked.
Return to service before evening.
— N.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: The glass cracked on Tuesday. Nell put it right yesterday.

choices.reply: The new relay has a different address. The saved routine still calls the old one.

choices.text: It was dark when I arrived.
choices.reply: She meant to have it done before then.
Yes. The slate only listens at arm’s length, so we’ll have to stand beside it.

pages.speaker: narration
pages.text: In smaller writing: landing-lamp. Two more names follow it: repair-light, assembly-light.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: Leave the stair light on. She’ll be carrying things when she comes back.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: The lantern is on the wall at the foot of the stairs. Hold the slate up to it and ask.

pages.speaker: narration
pages.text: The lantern warms from the centre out. Light catches the underside of the handrail.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: There.

pages.speaker: narration
pages.text: For a moment she says nothing else. There is a pencilled card beside the vice.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: She left the tables off while she was changing it. We used to bring them on together.

choices.reply: The long bench and the assembly table. The card has all three addresses.

choices.text: Did you write the old card?
choices.reply: Nell wrote it. I used to read out the names while she checked them.
I’ll stay here.

pages.speaker: narration
pages.text: The rest of the card is a short list. The last name has a check beside it; the first two have none.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: The screen on the wall reaches all three at once. You’ll have to stand at it, though.

pages.speaker: narration
pages.text: Under the work lights, the rubbed edges of Nell’s tools show silver. The little labels on the drawers can be read from the bench.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: That’s the morning round.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: Nell will want that routine kept.

choices.reply: Top one. She’ll look there first.
The gate light. Nell’s ticket is behind this one.
She said lunchtime. There’s another cup by the stove.

pages.speaker: narration
pages.text: Behind the workshop card is a complaint from the north gate. Nell has crossed out ‘lamp replaced’ and written only: ‘Again?’

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: That one came back yesterday.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: Oh. Morning.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: You’re the one in the loft, then? I’m Hotaru.

choices.reply: I heard your bag on the stairs. I thought Nell was moving things again.

choices.text: Nell said you could show me around.
choices.reply: Of course. She’s left a few things here for you. Have you found the paper drawer?

choices.text: Have you been asleep all week?
choices.reply: Most of it. Nell’s been taking the calls herself. Is it still morning?

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: Nell left you the desk. The drawers stick a little; lift them as you pull.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: There’s a work ticket downstairs. Nell should be back for lunch.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: She came up again after you’d gone to sleep. The board by the bed always gives her away.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: She left something on the quilt. Twelve inches by eight, set down very square.

choices.reply: I couldn’t say from here. It’s mostly one flat edge.
Only ‘there’. She says that when a thing is sitting right.
It hasn’t moved all night. I’d have heard.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: Pick it up before you go down. She didn’t leave it there for the bed’s benefit.

pages.speaker: narration
pages.text: It is lighter than it looks, and warm from the window. A grey cord trails from one edge and ends in a brass plug no thicker than a pencil.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: That’s the field slate. She used to carry it everywhere.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: She’d hold it against whatever was misbehaving and ask what the matter was.

choices.reply: Mostly it said ‘fault’, in capitals. Nell found that helpful.
The screen downstairs. There’s a socket under the glass, with a brass collar.
Was. She put it where you’d trip over it. That’s how she hands things over.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: It’s on the wall by the long bench. The only thing along there that isn’t wood.

pages.speaker: narration
pages.text: The street doors swing out onto warm cobbles. Somewhere below the wall, a tram bell rings once and stops.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: Four days since I was last out here. Someone’s chalked squares on the cobbles since then.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: And Bram’s painted his gate again. That makes three coats this month.

choices.reply: Next door. He builds things. Mostly that fence.
Until the twenty-to-eight comes up. Then it’s quiet with a tram in it.
Down to the square. Two hundred and twelve of them. I counted on the way down once, and on the way up to check.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: Nell comes back up that way with the bread. You hear the gate before you see her.

pages.speaker: narration
pages.text: The street drops its last few steps into the square. Awnings down one side, and the smell of bread.

pages.speaker: hotaru
pages.text: That’s the beacon in the middle. Nell stops there on the way back. Every time. I’ve counted.

pages.speaker: narration
pages.text: Under the glass a root glows the colour of strong tea. The needle on its dial sits low.

haverlund-lane: Mind the chalk squares. Somebody’s halfway through a game.
That’s Pepper on the wall. The notice says she doesn’t come when called. The notice is right.
The lamp by the gate has a wire all the way from the square. Nobody’s told it what to do yet.
The twenty-to-eight was late again. I could hear the bell from the shelf.
waiting-ticket: Nell pinned the ticket by the window.
The little drawer under the vice sticks. Mind your fingers.
landing-light: I’ll keep out of the way while you try it.
Nell left the fitting checked. The address is on her ticket.
morning-round: The two work lights belong on that card as well.
She usually starts at the long bench.
finished: There’s still warmth in the kettle.
haverlund-square: The clock’s been five minutes fast since spring. Nell still sets her watch by it.
That little one takes the parcels round. It waits for the handles to stop swinging before it goes.
You can smell the first batch from the top of the steps. Getting back up is harder.

haverlund-lane.title: Out on the lane
haverlund-lane.hint: Nell’s jobs are pinned on the board inside. Nothing out here has a ticket yet.

haverlund-square.title: Rootward Square
haverlund-square.hint: The square is open to explore. Nell’s work tickets are still on the board back at the workshop.

tablet_waiting.title: Something on the quilt
tablet_waiting.hint: Nell left it on your bed. Hotaru thinks it is meant for you.
